steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: ...Hello.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: I'm pretty sure I know what you're going to say. But go ahead and say it.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: It's on me then.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: I suspect that Catastrophe Messenger Biederman was the mastermind behind all of this.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: This is the only assessment I can make based upon the extreme scarcity of physical evidence.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I've seen your evidence. Biederman was a Contingency Contract Catastrophe Messenger.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Rhodes Island has worked with them a lot, and they have contributed substantially to the fight against Catastrophes.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: But that doesn't mean they're all so 'benevolent.'

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: Speaking from experience as a bodyguard for Catastrophe Messengers, you are correct.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: After the Catastrophe struck Wolumonde, Biederman made the determination that the town could not be saved.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: In order to save as many lives as possible, he decided to assassinate a Rhodes Island operator and draw the attention of the outside world. Totally feasible.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: But would Contingency Contract really sit by and let this happen? They should have some kind of standard.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: The Contingency Contract is merely platform for offering up bounties and accomplishing goals. What goes on behind the scenes, no one knows.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: But there is a small group of Catastrophe Messengers with rather extreme beliefs that conflate Catastrophes with man-made disasters. If you'll excuse the turn of phrase, they're a bunch of sick utilitarians.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: As long as it frees people from the fear of Catastrophes... No, they're not even interested in helping people. It's all about fighting some ancient, imaginary enemy they call 'Catastrophes.'

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: No action is too rash for them.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: And now they've taken up root in this well-regulated contractual mechanism. They're far more entrenched than I had previously thought.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: But... herein lies the problem.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: This overreaction was predicated on a belief in Rhodes Island. The belief that Folinic would come looking for Atro.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: I don't know by what means this madman used the Contingency Contract, but I do know one thing for certain.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: He would not hinge his entire plan on 'feelings.' In their eyes, what we do is something akin to acting out a fable.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: To bet everything on Rhodes Island's bonds with its operators... is very strange.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...It's all just speculation.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: This makes sense.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: —That thing in your hand, is that a 'Gramophone' core?

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: This is the only physical evidence of the scale of the fire. It was undoubtedly started by overloading this core.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: But Biederman... wasn't Leithanian.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Even if he could somehow get his hands on this core... He... would not have been able to master the Originium Arts that caused it to overload and incinerate those people.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: He'd only been here for half a year. Not to mention the L-44 'Gramophone' system is a rather new product.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: If he really learned how to do this is in such a short time, he should have gone to the Central University and joined one of the Spires.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Yes. Even now, we're still not sure who the real killer is.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Aside from the collection of disasters that devastated our town and made our jobs even more difficult...

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: ...We have nothing.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Let's not be too quick to lose hope. These are all pretty shallow inferences.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Do Folinic and Suzuran know about this? So much has happened, but they're the ones who would be affected the most by this.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: ...Honestly, I don't know how to break the news to them.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Miss Folinic has been struggling to accept the emptiness of her vengeance. That may be selfish, but it's what's best for everyone.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: ...Or, we can continue searching for the truth.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Most of the rebels have been arrested. Others left with Mudrock. But there are still some out there protesting. After all that, no one's in much of a mood for trouble.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: But the jail isn't in good shape. Not to mention, the riots also damaged a lot of supplies. Rations are getting even tighter.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Now then... how is Tatjana?

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: She was under a lot of stress to begin with. Seeing that snapped her. The psychological damage is a lot more serious than her mild burns.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: I see... That's my fault... *cough* *cough*——*hack* *cough*!

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: If we continue down this road, it's only going to cause more conflict.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: You have long since given up on the truth.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: If you had these doubts from the beginning, but still went along with it, that only means...

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: No. Let me be clear about one thing. Biederman is still the prime suspect from all the information we have so far.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: And these two questions about the means and his ability do not clear him. The evidence still points to him.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: I cannot deny that. At the end of the day, it is possible that Contingency Contract may have some methods we are not aware of.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: The truth still eludes us.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: I had given up on pursuing any truth when they told me I couldn't have a funeral for my son.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: As for what I really want?

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: I just want... the survivors to at least... be able to... *cough* *cough*, *cough* *cough* *cough*—!

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: If that's what you really want, you should go to Rhodes Island for an examination.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: You're trembling.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: It's no secret that I still have some... fear... of the Infected.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Fear...? Hah. You fought that hard for all of us and it turns out you're afraid of the Infected?

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Maybe Rhodes Island really is trustworthy.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: Oh, about your infection... I think Folinic wanted to ask...

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: When did it happen?

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: If I had known you were so hostile to the Infected, Miss GreyThroat, I probably wouldn't have hidden it.

steps.name: GreyThroat
steps.text: I'm the one who should be sorry. I've... gotten used to my fear.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: When those old Winterwisp clansmen were out there killing nobles and merchants, I was out there hunting them.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: The last of them had set up camp by the lake. He knew I was coming. I guess he spotted my shadow. And he stabbed me in the chest with a chunk of Originium.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: He was Infected too.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Yes... Yes, he was. I couldn't finish him off. I thought he was planning to fight to the death, but his and my revenge both came to an end.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: The look on his face at the last moment before we tumbled into the lake together was very... strange.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: It was like... regret. That old man was self-conscious of the relief he felt.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: Just like how he sang his life away while we fought Reunion and the insurgents. Kind of frustrating.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: He... he died. Oripathy had failed to take him over the years. The last proper Winterwisp clansman, the aboriginal people of this land, had died.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: The Infected split from us, and the populace could no longer stand the absurdity of the nobles. They rose up.

steps.name: Severin
steps.text: And that's where it ended.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: Miss Tatjana!

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: Oh... it's you.

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: I'm so glad... you're alright...

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: You look much better.

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: Hehe... maybe I really do push myself too hard, if I'm always falling down at times like this.

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: I've been... forcing myself not to think about Thor. But his smile... his pain... the fire burning his body...

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: I'm sorry. I'm doing it again.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: It's okay.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: We both... know.

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: But at least the killer paid for what he did.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Maybe.

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: Miss Folinic?

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: No... never mind...

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: But Wolumonde... still has a lot of problems ahead of her...

steps.name: Tatjana
steps.text: First and foremost, the Infected...

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I'm sorry. I actually knew about Mr. Severin's condition. He asked me not to tell anyone.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: I should have told everyone as soon as he talked about using Originium Arts to operate the refrigeration unit in the control room.

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: But... He's in a lot of pain too. Everyone is.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Those who couldn't bear it... have already been thrown in jail.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: The rest... are just like me.

steps.name: Click
steps.text: Everyone! Over here!

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: The route has been mapped out, and I believe a small group could make it back to Rhodes Island safely.

steps.name: Click
steps.text: Wow, that was an unforgettable experience. Should I document it? Or try to forget it anyway?

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: Just don't use it to make money.

steps.name: Click
steps.text: Give me a little credit!

steps.name: Suzuran
steps.text: This route... Would this route allow the people of Wolumonde to evacuate safely?

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: Hard to say... That's a lot of people, with even more wounded and prisoners. You can't leave the prisoners to die.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Right. Where's GreyThroat?

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: She... left. She had to see someone.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: She'll join us later.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Oh? I'll go get her.

steps.name: Ayerscarpe
steps.text: There's no need for—

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: No... There is.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: I'm going to get her.

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: We should elect a new Schultz at once!

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: But after all he's done for us, we shouldn't be so fickle.

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: E-even so, we can't let an Infected wander the streets in broad daylight.

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: We should decide after we see the results of Schultz Severin's medical examination. He might...

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: No matter what the examination says, we can't have an Infected leading us! What will the nobles say?

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: Would tourists or merchants come to a town patrolled by an Infected?

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: Hey! Hey!

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: Outpost reports a convoy approaching! They're flying a Gendarmerie flag!

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: L-let's go see if the receiver still works. We have to confirm their IFF——
In the midst of the crowd's debate, the former Schultz, Severin Hawthorn himself, has long since fallen asleep from exhaustion.
He dreams of the moon moving forward across a shining plain, and women look up to the stars while men rebuild the towers.
He dreams that a giant rises out of the earth, his fallen son, and the giant casts away all the calamities, filling up the sundered land with its godlike power.
He dreams of the giant lifting his town onto his shoulders, carrying it toward the melting ice.
He dreams of songs floating on the wind, of the earth speaking, of Originium sinking back into the ground, and Oripathy disappearing from the world.
He dreams that the giant is Winterwisp, snow and water, the cradle of community, savagery, and civilization. He dreams that the giant stands firm.
He is tired, and his violent bronchial spasms do not bring him back to reality.
He continues to dream of leaning against his sickle, looking out over fields of golden wheat.
He laughs in his dream, until he weeps.
It is the first time he's cried since losing his son.
